mainTopic: Sinking the כיור overnight, בן קטין's machine, and the minimum water for the כיור
overview: The גמרא first says that the difference between two views on the כיור's water is the rabbinic decree to keep it sunk all night. It then challenges this from רבי יוחנן's rule that a כהן who washed for תרומת הדשן before dawn need not wash again the next day. That causes no problem for רבא, but for אביי it seems to make רבי contradict himself. The answer is that the כיור is lifted out for the washing and then sunk again before dawn, so its water stays fit. That answer makes רבי יוחנן sound like רב חסדא, and the גמרא explains that they differ only on whether keeping the כיור sunk all night is a מצוה. A משנה about the sound of בן קטין's machine is brought against רב חסדא. The גמרא answers that the sound came from lowering the כיור with a wheel in the morning, which served as a signal alongside גביני the crier. Finally, the גמרא turns to רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's rule that a כיור must hold enough water for four כהנים, and begins a challenge from a ברייתא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The difference is the decree to sink the basin
steps.stepSummary: The practical difference between the two views is the rabbinic decree to sink the כיור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is the decree of sinking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question it asked just before this: what practical difference is there between the two views about the כיור's water? The answer is the rabbinic decree to sink the כיור overnight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On one view, the water becomes unfit if it is lifted at any point during the night. On the other view, it becomes unfit only if it is lifted at dawn. Even so, the חכמים decreed that the כיור stay sunk all night, so no one lifts it at dawn by mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them
A rabbinic decree made as a safeguard
Sinking (lowering the כיור into its pit)
The Basin that the כהנים washed from

phrases.english: There is a difference between them:
the decree of sinking.
phrases.notes: This means sinking the כיור into its pit overnight so its water stays connected to the ground.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the earlier question of what the practical difference between the two opinions is.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: On one view the water becomes unfit only at dawn, yet the כיור is still sunk all night because of a rabbinic decree.

steps.title: Challenge from washing for the ash removal
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן said that washing for תרומת הדשן before dawn still counts for the next day.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי יוחנן said: if a כהן washed his hands for the removal of the ashes, he does not need to wash again the next day, because he already washed at the start of the service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that the כיור must stay sunk all night. It quotes another statement of רבי יוחנן that seems to point the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תרומת הדשן was done before dawn, and the washing for it was done from the כיור. If that washing still counts for the whole next day, then the כיור was in use before dawn. That seems to clash with keeping it sunk all night.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he say? (opens a challenge)
The כהן's washing of his hands and feet before service
Removing ashes from the מזבח, the first service of the day
The start of the day's service

steps.confusionAlert: Although תרומת הדשן takes place before dawn, it counts as the start of the next day's service. That is why the washing for it carries over.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
if he sanctified his hands for the removal of the ashes,
the next day he does not need to sanctify again,
because he already sanctified at the beginning of the service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the requirement to keep the כיור sunk all night.
steps.kashyaTarget: The decree that the כיור must stay sunk the entire night
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Washing before dawn for תרומת הדשן counts for the next day, so the כיור seems to be used before dawn rather than kept sunk.

steps.title: No problem according to רבא
steps.stepSummary: According to רבא, the two statements follow different תנאים, so they do not conflict.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for רבא, who explained that statement according to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון; this one follows רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the challenge is easy to answer according to רבא. This step sets up the real problem, which comes in the next step for אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבא explained רבי יוחנן's washing rule according to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who holds that washing does not lose its effect overnight. The sinking decree follows רבי, who holds that dawn ends it. Two different תנאים, so there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well for... (sets up a contrast with 'but for X...')
He explains it as following a certain opinion

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rava,
who explains that statement
phrases.notes: "That statement" means רבי יוחנן's rule about washing for תרומת הדשן.

phrases.english: according to Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon,
this one follows Rabbi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge according to רבא as a setup for the problem according to אביי.
steps.kashyaTarget: The challenge from step 2, examined according to each אמורא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For רבא, the two rules come from different תנאים, so the contradiction disappears.

steps.title: For אביי, רבי contradicts himself
steps.stepSummary: According to אביי, both rules follow רבי, so his two positions clash.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to אביי, who explains it according to רבי, there is a contradiction between רבי and רבי: why must the כיור be sunk there, but not here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises the real difficulty. According to אביי, רבי seems to hold two rules that do not fit together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי explained the washing rule according to רבי. So רבי holds that washing before dawn carries over to the next day, and no sinking is needed. Yet רבי also requires the כיור to be sunk all night, so the גמרא asks what the difference is.

keyTerms.meaning: But (introduces the side where there is a problem)
A contradiction between two statements of רבי
What is different?
Sinks it

steps.whatToRemember: The decree to sink the כיור follows רבי. For רבא this is no problem, but for אביי it contradicts רבי's own rule that washing for תרומת הדשן carries over to the next day.

phrases.english: But according to Abaye, who explains it according to Rabbi,
there is a contradiction between Rabbi and Rabbi:
what is different there, that one sinks it,
phrases.notes: "There" means the כיור overnight, which must be sunk.

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאי שְׁנָא הָכָא דְּלָא מְשַׁקַּע לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: and what is different here, that one does not sink it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the contrast: no problem for רבא, but a contradiction for אביי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's two positions, according to אביי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If washing before dawn counts for the next day without sinking, why does רבי require the כיור to be sunk all night?

steps.title: The Basin is lifted and then sunk again
steps.stepSummary: The clash is resolved: the כיור is lifted out for washing and then sunk again, so its water does not become unfit at dawn.
steps.simpleTranslation: He lifts the כיור out and then sinks it back again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from the last step. It shows how רבי יוחנן's ruling can work even under the rule that the water in the כיור becomes unfit overnight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that a כיור raised at night for washing would have unfit water by dawn. The answer is that it is only raised for a short time and then sunk back down before dawn. So the water is still fit, and the washing done at night can still count for the next day.

keyTerms.meaning: lifts out, removes
sinks (the כיור back into its pit of water)
the Basin in the Temple used for washing hands and feet

phrases.english: That he lifts it out and then sinks it again.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the כיור. Sinking it is what keeps its water from becoming unfit overnight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the clash that step 4 raised in רבי's view (according to אביי).
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the case narrowly: the כיור is raised for a short time and then sunk again before dawn.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Raising the כיור at night means its water becomes unfit by morning, so washing at night could not count for the next day.
steps.terutzMaskana: The כיור goes back into its pit before dawn, so the water stays fit.

steps.title: Then why can't he wash again the next day?
steps.stepSummary: If the water stays fit, why would רבי יוחנן say the כהן does not sanctify his hands and feet the next day?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does it say 'the next day he does not sanctify'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. If the water is still fine, it sounds odd that the כהן is told not to wash with it the next day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'אינו מקדש' sound like a ban, as if washing again would be wrong. A ban would make sense only if the water were unfit. Since the last step said the water stays fit, the wording now looks strange.

keyTerms.meaning: if so
sanctifies, meaning washes his hands and feet from the כיור
why?

phrases.english: If so, 'the next day he does not sanctify' —
why?
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are part of the corrected wording.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 5 using the wording of רבי יוחנן's statement from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording 'למחר אינו מקדש' in רבי יוחנן's statement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the water was never made unfit, there is no reason to forbid washing with it again.

steps.title: He doesn't need to, but he may
steps.stepSummary: The wording means the כהן does not need to wash again. It does not mean he is forbidden to.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means: he does not need to sanctify.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by reading רבי יוחנן's words more gently. 'He does not sanctify' means it is not needed, not that it is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The washing he did at night already counts for the whole next day of service. So a second washing is simply extra. Nothing is wrong with the water.

keyTerms.meaning: does not need to

phrases.english: He does not need to sanctify.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads the wording: 'does not' means 'need not'.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אינו מקדש' is a ban on washing again.
steps.terutzMaskana: Washing again is not needed, but it is allowed.

steps.title: Isn't this just רב חסדא's view?
steps.stepSummary: If water in a כיור that was lifted and sunk again stays fit, then רבי יוחנן seems to be saying exactly what רב חסדא said.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are you saying the water is fit for the מתירין? That is the same as רב חסדא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the answer has made רבי יוחנן's view the same as רב חסדא's. If so, why would both statements be needed?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 implied that a כיור lifted at night and sunk again before dawn still has fit water. That water could then be used to wash before the מתירין, the main service that makes the offering permitted. That is the same idea as רב חסדא's earlier ruling, so the two statements look like one rule said twice.

keyTerms.meaning: is this to say?
the parts of the service that make the offering permitted (such as placing the blood)
that is the same as

phrases.english: Is this to say that it is fit for the permitting parts of the service?!
phrases.notes: 'It' is the water of a כיור that was lifted at night and sunk again before dawn.

phrases.english: That is the same as רב חסדא!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from the answer in step 5 and challenges it as repeating רב חסדא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The difference between רבי יוחנן's view and רב חסדא's.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both hold that lifting and sinking again before dawn keeps the water fit, the two statements say the same thing.

steps.title: They differ on a מצוה to keep it sunk
steps.stepSummary: The two views differ over whether there is a מצוה to keep the כיור sunk throughout the night.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is the מצוה of sinking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the two views are not identical. They agree the water stays fit, but they disagree about a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that lifting the כיור and sinking it again before dawn keeps the water fit. רבי יוחנן holds that, from the start, there is a מצוה to keep the כיור sunk all night. רב חסדא holds that there is no such מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: there is a difference between them
the מצוה of sinking the כיור

steps.whatToRemember: The water of a כיור that was lifted and sunk again before dawn stays fit. רבי יוחנן and רב חסדא differ only on whether keeping it sunk all night is a מצוה from the start.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי יוחנן says the water becomes unfit just because the כיור was lifted during the night. As long as it is sunk again before dawn, the water stays fit. The disagreement with רב חסדא is only about the ideal way to do it (a מצוה), not about whether the water is fit.

phrases.english: The difference between them is the מצוה of sinking.
phrases.notes: According to רבי יוחנן, keeping the כיור sunk all night is a מצוה. רב חסדא does not hold of that מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8 by naming a practical difference between רבי יוחנן and רב חסדא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Names a practical difference between the two views.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן and רב חסדא say exactly the same thing.
steps.terutzMaskana: They agree the water stays fit, but they differ over a מצוה to keep the כיור sunk all night.

steps.title: The noise of בן קטין's machine suggests the כיור was sunk all night
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says the כהנים heard the sound of בן קטין's wooden machine for the כיור each morning. The גמרא assumes this was the sound of lifting the כיור up, which would mean it had been sunk all night. That goes against רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: The כהנים would not see the כהן who cleared the ashes and would not hear his voice, until they heard the sound of the wooden machine that בן קטין made for the כיור. Then they would say: The time has come to wash hands and feet from the כיור. Isn't this the sound of lifting the כיור up? So it must have been sunk during the night!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to attack רב חסדא, who said there is no מצוה to keep the כיור sunk overnight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each morning a machine noise signaled that washing could begin. If that noise came from raising the כיור, then it had been sunk all night, which suggests sinking it overnight was the normal practice. That seems to contradict רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: A machine or device; here, the one בן קטין built for the כיור
A כהן גדול who made improvements to the כיור
Lifts up or removes
Sinks or submerges

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
They would not see him
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the כהן who went in early to clear the ashes from the מזבח.

phrases.english: and would not hear his voice,
until they would hear the sound of the wood
that בן קטין made into a machine for the כיור,
and they would say:

phrases.aramaic: הִגִּיעַ [עֵת] קִידּוּשׁ יָדַיִם וְרַגְלַיִם מִן הַכִּיּוֹר.
phrases.english: The time of washing hands and feet from the כיור has arrived.
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets, 'time,' is part of the corrected wording.

phrases.english: What, is it not that he lifts it up?
Evidently he sinks it during the night!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the position from Step 9 that, according to רב חסדא, there is no מצוה to keep the כיור sunk overnight.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's view that the כיור need not be sunk overnight
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The morning noise came from raising the כיור, so it had been sunk all night as standard practice.

steps.title: The noise was from lowering the כיור, not raising it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the sound came from sinking the כיור in the morning after it had been up all night.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the noise is from sinking it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב חסדא by reading the משנה differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the כיור stayed up all night and was lowered in the morning, the משנה gives no proof that it was sunk overnight. So רב חסדא is not contradicted.

keyTerms.meaning: No; this rejects the assumption of the question

phrases.english: No, it is that he sinks it.
phrases.notes: In this reading, the כיור was up all night and gets lowered in the morning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of Step 10 by flipping which action made the noise.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The noise was from raising a כיור that had been sunk all night.
steps.terutzMaskana: The noise was from lowering the כיור in the morning.

steps.title: Would lowering the כיור make any noise?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how lowering the כיור could be loud enough to hear, since lowering takes no effort or machinery.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he is sinking it, would its sound be heard?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer just given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Raising a heavy כיור needs a machine and makes noise, but letting it down seems easy and quiet. So how could the משנה describe a sound everyone heard?

keyTerms.meaning: Would it be heard? (a rhetorical question expecting 'no')
Its sound

phrases.english: If it is that he sinks it,
would its sound be heard?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי דִּמְשַׁקַּע לֵיהּ מִי מִשְׁתְּמַע קָלֵיהּ
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the noise came from lowering the כיור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Lowering needs no machine, so it would not make a noticeable sound.

steps.title: He lowered it with a wheel
steps.stepSummary: The כיור was lowered using a wheel, and the wheel made the sound.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sinks it with a wheel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that even the lowering was done with the wheel, so it made noise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the כיור could be lowered without machinery, it was in fact lowered with the wheel. That explains the sound in the משנה, and רב חסדא still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A wheel

phrases.english: He sinks it with a wheel.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Lowering is done quietly by hand.
steps.terutzMaskana: Lowering was done with a wheel, which made noise.

steps.title: Another version: the wheel was used on purpose as a signal
steps.stepSummary: A second version of the answer says the כיור was lowered with its wheel on purpose, so the sound would call the כהנים to come.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: He sinks it with its wheel so that its sound will be heard, and the כהנים will hear and come.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the answer, adding a reason for using the noisy wheel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first version just said a wheel was used. This version explains why: the noise was meant as a signal that the day's service was starting.

keyTerms.meaning: Another version of the discussion
Its wheel (the device that lowered the כיור)
So that

phrases.english: Another version:
He sinks it with its wheel,
so that its sound will be heard
and they will hear and come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the answer in Steps 12-13, with a purpose for the noise.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The noise was just a side effect of lowering.
steps.terutzMaskana: The noise was made on purpose to call the כהנים.

steps.title: Why need a noise signal if גביני the crier called them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a noise signal was needed if גביני the crier already called the כהנים to the service.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there was גביני the crier!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second version: there was already a person whose job was to call the כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If גביני the crier announced the service, a second signal from the wheel seems unnecessary. So why say the wheel was used on purpose to call them?

keyTerms.meaning: גביני the crier, who called the כהנים to the service
But surely (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: But there was גביני the crier!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the purpose given in Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the wheel noise was meant to call the כהנים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A crier already did that job, so a second signal seems pointless.

steps.title: There were two signals, and either one brought the כהנים
steps.stepSummary: There were two signals, the crier and the wheel. Whoever heard either one would come.
steps.simpleTranslation: They would make two signals. Whoever heard this one would come, and whoever heard that one would come.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that both signals were used so that every כהן would hear at least one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The crier did not make the wheel unnecessary. Using two signals made sure no כהן missed the start of the service.

keyTerms.meaning: Signals or markers
Comes

steps.whatToRemember: The objection from בן קטין's machine does not disprove רב חסדא. The noise came from lowering the כיור in the morning with a wheel, and according to one version it was one of two signals calling the כהנים.

phrases.english: They would make two signals;
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording.

phrases.english: whoever heard from this one would come,
and whoever heard from that one would come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15 and closes the discussion about the machine.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The crier made the wheel signal pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both signals were used so everyone would hear one of them.

steps.title: A כיור must hold enough water for four כהנים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to an earlier statement: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא rules that a כיור without enough water for four כהנים to wash may not be used. The source is the פסוק about משה, אהרן and his sons.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the matter itself. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: Any כיור that does not have enough water for four כהנים to wash from it may not be used for washing, as it says: 'And משה and אהרן and his sons washed from it.'
steps.whatsHappening: With the word גופא, the גמרא goes back to a statement quoted earlier and starts discussing it on its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק lists משה, אהרן and his sons washing from the כיור, which comes to four people (משה, אהרן, and his two sons). From this, רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא learns that a כיור is only valid if it holds enough water for four כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself': going back to a statement quoted earlier
The basin the כהנים washed their hands and feet from
To sanctify, meaning to wash hands and feet before the service
'And they washed from it'

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a minimum size for the water in the כיור, and the גמרא will now analyze this rule.

phrases.english: The matter itself:
רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said:
Any כיור that does not have in it
enough for four כהנים to wash from it,
one may not wash with it,
as it is said:
'And משה and אהרן and his sons washed from it, etc.'

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion about sinking the כיור and returns to a statement quoted earlier, to examine it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כיור that cannot supply enough water for four כהנים to wash may not be used for washing.

steps.title: A ברייתא says any vessel may be used for washing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא. The ברייתא says כהנים may wash their hands and feet from all vessels, even ones that hold only a רביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא raises a challenge: a ברייתא teaches that the כהנים may wash their hands and feet from any vessel, even one that holds a רביעית of water...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a challenge against the rule from Step 17 by quoting a ברייתא. The quote is not finished yet. The ברייתא keeps going in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said a כיור that cannot hold water for four כהנים may not be used. This ברייתא seems to allow washing from any vessel, even a tiny one that holds a רביעית. Small amounts like that are far less than four כהנים need, so the two sources seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: All the vessels
They wash and make holy, meaning the כהנים wash their hands and feet before the עבודה
A quarter-לוג, a small measure of liquid

steps.confusionAlert: Here מְקַדְּשִׁין does not mean making something הקדש. It means the washing of hands and feet that a כהן must do before the עבודה.

phrases.english: They raised a challenge: All vessels may be used to sanctify,
phrases.notes: This starts a ברייתא. 'Sanctify' means washing hands and feet before the עבודה.

phrases.english: whether they hold a quarter-log,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rule of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא that was stated in Step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's rule that a כיור without water for four כהנים may not be used
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא allows washing from all vessels, even ones that hold only a small amount like a רביעית. This seems to contradict a minimum of water for four כהנים.
